identity.description:
Run pr-review in CI on every pull request

## Summary

Each pull request in this repo now gets an automated review from pr-review. The review runs when a PR opens, gets a push, reopens or becomes ready. A maintainer can also start it with a `review:` label or the comment `@pr-review full`. It posts one review comment and one neutral check run. It does not block a merge. A draft PR gets no review until it is marked ready.

**Ticket:** N/A
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

The "Set up CI" section of the `jerridan/pr-review` README owns this setup. No `docs/design.md` section or crew reference governs it.

### What changed, by file

- `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` — new. It is the consumer workflow from the pr-review README, word for word. It calls `jerridan/pr-review/.github/workflows/review.yml@v1` with `secrets: inherit`.
- `.pr-review/config.yaml` — new. It sets `skip.draft: true`, so the run skips a draft PR. The `ready_for_review` event then starts the review.

### Constraints that applied

- Version bump: none. The file is not under `agents/`, `skills/`, `hooks/` or the manifests, so it does not reach a plugin user.
- Secret: the repo secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` exists (set 2026-10-15).
- Access: this repo is public, so it can call only a public workflow. `jerridan/pr-review` is now public.
- Release tag: the tag `v1` exists on `jerridan/pr-review`.

### How this was verified

I checked the secret with `gh secret list`, the access setting with `gh api /repos/jerridan/pr-review/actions/permissions/access`, and the tag with `gh api repos/jerridan/pr-review/git/refs/tags/v1`. This PR is the first run of the workflow. Its result shows on this PR.

### Known gaps

- `pull_request_target` and `issue_comment` events read the workflow from the default branch. The label and comment triggers work only after this PR merges.
- pr-review reads `.pr-review/config.yaml` from the base branch. The draft skip starts to work only after this PR merges, so this draft PR still gets a review.
- The records branch `pr-review-records` does not exist yet. The first run creates it.

findings.claim: The description says only a maintainer can start the review with a label or comment, but the workflow does not check the author or association on these triggers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `if:` check on author_association, or state that the called workflow gates the trigger.
findings.explanation: Any commenter can fire the workflow with inherited secrets, unless the reusable workflow does the check.

findings.claim: The description does not mention that the workflow grants `contents: write`, which a reader needs to know because the run writes to the repo (records branch).
findings.suggested_fix: State the permissions in the description.
findings.explanation: The write access to the repo contents is not disclosed in the description.

findings.claim: The workflow has no concurrency group, so quick pushes or a label plus a push start reviews that overlap and post duplicate comments or check runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `concurrency: { group: pr-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`.
findings.explanation: Several triggers can fire for the same PR, and nothing cancels a run that is already in progress.

findings.claim: The workflow has no concurrency group, so runs that overlap on rapid pushes can each post a review and a check run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a concurrency group keyed on the PR number with cancel-in-progress: true, unless the reusable workflow already sets one.
findings.explanation: Each synchronize event starts a new run, and nothing cancels the run that is still going.

findings.claim: The workflow passes every repo secret, with contents: write, to a third-party reusable workflow pinned to the mutable tag v1, on pull_request_target and issue_comment triggers.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin to a commit SHA, pass only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN explicitly, and drop contents: write if the review does not need it.
findings.explanation: Anyone who can move the v1 tag or push to that repo runs code with write access and every secret, in a privileged trigger context.

findings.claim: The workflow does not check who wrote a comment before the issue_comment trigger starts it, so any commenter on this public repo can start a run that uses the secrets.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `if:` on the job that requires author_association OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR.
findings.explanation: If the called workflow does not check author_association, anyone can spend the token or trigger a privileged run.

findings.claim: The workflow grants contents: write even though the PR says the review only posts a comment and a check run.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove contents: write, or explain in a comment why the run needs it.
findings.explanation: This gives broader write access than a comment and a check run need. It may exist only so the run can create the records branch.

findings.claim: The workflow passes every repo secret to a third-party reusable workflow pinned to a mutable tag, so whoever controls that tag gets the secrets.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the reusable workflow to a full commit SHA and pass only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, not secrets: inherit.
findings.explanation: If someone moves the v1 tag, new code runs with all secrets and write permissions.

findings.claim: pull_request_target and issue_comment runs have base-repo secrets and write tokens, and the caller does not check who triggered them, so fork PR content or any commenter can drive a privileged run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an if: condition that requires author_association to be OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR for issue_comment, and do not check out untrusted head code with secrets.
findings.explanation: On a public repo anyone can comment, and the run then uses inherited secrets and a contents: write token.

findings.claim: The job grants contents: write, which lets it push to the repo during runs that handle untrusted PR input.
findings.suggested_fix: Grant contents: read, or move the records-branch writes to a separate job with tighter control.
findings.explanation: A broad write token makes a prompt-injected or compromised review much more damaging.

findings.claim: The workflow runs on pull_request_target and issue_comment with `secrets: inherit` and write permissions. This can expose the repo secrets and a write token to an untrusted fork PR or to any commenter.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass only the secret the job needs, and gate issue_comment on author_association (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR). Do not check out the PR head code in a privileged job.
findings.explanation: These triggers run in the base repo's context with secrets. The workflow does no author or association check, so the safety depends wholly on the gating in the called workflow.

findings.claim: `secrets: inherit` passes every repo secret to the third-party workflow, not only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
findings.explanation: Passing every secret gives the external code more access than it needs.

findings.claim: The reusable workflow is pinned to the mutable tag v1, not to a commit SHA.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the workflow to a full commit SHA.
findings.explanation: Someone can move the tag to new code, and that code then runs with the repo's secrets and write token.

findings.claim: The job gets `contents: write`, so the external workflow can push to any branch, the default branch included, and not only to the records branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the records in a separate repo or as artifacts, or limit the write access with branch protection.
findings.explanation: This permission is wider than a review needs, and it adds to the damage if the external workflow is compromised.

finding.claim: The job gets `contents: write`, so the external workflow can push to any branch, the default branch included, and not only to the records branch.
finding.suggested_fix: Keep the records in a separate repo or as artifacts, or limit the write access with branch protection.
finding.explanation: This permission is wider than a review needs, and it adds to the damage if the external workflow is compromised.

first.rationale: The `contents: write` line is real, but the description says the first run creates the `pr-review-records` branch, which needs that permission. It also says the file is the README's consumer workflow word for word. The finding's claim that the permission is wider than a review needs is therefore not supported, and the suggested fix is generic.

escalated.rationale: The claim is true. A GITHUB_TOKEN with `contents: write` can push to any unprotected branch, and this job grants it to an external workflow pinned to the mutable `@v1` tag, which also runs on `pull_request_target`. But the pr-review README asks for this permission so the tool can write its records branch, so this is a least-privilege hardening suggestion, not a bug.
